title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-06-05
source: 7 Inch Half Track Reel Master @ 7.5 ips(Recorded In Venue By Bear on a Sony 770 Reel 2 Reel)-1st Generation Cassettes Transferred By Dick Latvala(Master Reel Playback on a Technics 1506 Reel 2 Reel-Tascam 122 MK111 Cassette Deck no Dolby); Analog to Digital Transfer(Cassettes played back on Nakamichi Dragon-Sony PCM-R500 DAT @ 44.1KHz by Jim Wise circa late 1990's); Zero Gen DAT play back on a Sony PCM R-500-Digital Out @ 16/44.1kHz-Digital Audio Labs Card deluxe-WAV @ 16/44.1KHz; Editing(Adobe Audition CC)-Mastering & Processing(iZotope Ozone 6)-FLAC encoding(dBpoweramp)-Tagging(Tag & Re-name) JW:February 2015

ai_review.summary: Clear mic‑recorded tape with solid detail, highlighted by a smashing St. Stephen, buttery Hard to Handle and acoustic I Know You Riders.
ai_review.review: The recording is a stage‑mic capture that sounds surprisingly clean and detailed despite some drum‑mic overload and occasional speaker boominess. Musically the show shines – the band tears through St. Stephen with intensity, delivers a smooth Hard to Handle after a rough start, and treats fans to a lovely acoustic I Know You Riders. A few blemishes (a cut on Cryptical and feedback in The Other One) don’t detract from an overall strong mid‑1970 performance.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise both the musical set (standout songs, energetic playing) and the surprisingly good recording quality; minor technical flaws are noted but do not outweigh the positives.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Stage‑mic (not true audience or soundboard) with slight speaker boominess and drums a bit loud; occasional monitor feedback and a cut on Cryptical, but overall clear, well‑EQ'd and detailed.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A solid mid‑1970 set that rolls smoothly, delivering strong early acoustic work and building into high‑energy rock numbers; the second half maintains momentum despite minor hiccups.

band_member_comments.Bob: Bob (Bobby) is heard screaming "GODDAMMIT!" during a feedback moment in The Other One.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drums are mic'd too loud, contributing to a slightly boomy sound and occasional overload.
